items.question: What effect does the completed mantra and mudra rite produce on the targeted woman?
premises: The preceding verses prescribe drawing the love-syllable, binding the kṣobhiṇī mudrā, and reciting the vidyā one hundred and eight times.
The verse states that thereafter the woman becomes agitated and sidelong-glancing.
The verse states that she is tormented by the arrow of the bodiless god of love.
items.inference: The ritual sequence produces erotic agitation and attraction in the targeted woman.
uncertainties: The exact grammatical analysis and intended sense of pāṅgā are uncertain in this context.
The syntactic relation of the accusative anaṅgaśarapīḍitām to the nominative forms is not fully explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Then she becomes agitated, casting sidelong glances, tormented by the arrow of the bodiless god of love.
